branches.description: Trace promise from Genesis into Romans and Galatians.
branches.label: Follow promise

branches.description: Hold Genesis 22 with its later reception in Hebrews and James.
branches.label: Follow testing

character.centerRule: Abraham remains the stable human center; relationships and later Scripture uses must stay attached to inspectable source Scenes.

phases.orientation: Abram enters through a family line, leaves Haran, crosses Canaan, builds altars, and goes down to Egypt under famine.
phases.title: Origins and call

phases.orientation: Land, wealth, kinship, conflict, separation, rescue, and encounters with kings gather around Abram.
phases.title: Land and neighbors

phases.orientation: Promise is spoken beside childlessness, Hagar and Ishmael enter the household story, and Abram receives a new name and covenant sign.
phases.title: Promise and household

phases.orientation: Abraham receives visitors, hears renewed speech about Sarah, presses questions about Sodom, and moves through its aftermath and Gerar.
phases.title: Hospitality and intercession

phases.orientation: Isaac is born, Hagar and Ishmael depart, a treaty is made, and Abraham is tested with the son named in the promise.
phases.title: Sons and testing

phases.orientation: Sarah dies, Abraham obtains burial ground, Rebekah joins Isaac, inheritance is ordered, and Abraham dies and is buried.
phases.title: Loss and final years

phases.orientation: Isaac, Jacob, Torah, histories, prayer, poetry, prophets, and later Jewish writings remember Abraham through oath, ancestry, friendship, and promise.
phases.title: Family and Israel remember

phases.orientation: Genealogies, speeches, parables, disputes, and letters invoke Abraham in distinct arguments about ancestry, promise, faith, action, and hope.
phases.title: Gospel and apostolic memory

character.throughline: Abram becomes Abraham while country, land, altars, wealth, kin, kings, covenant, household conflict, sons, testing, grief, property, inheritance, death, and later memory gather around the same person.

points.label: actors and departure
points.left: Abram is named with Nahor and Haran before Terah’s household moves from Ur toward Canaan and settles in Haran.
points.right: The LORD commands Abram to leave, speaks blessing, and Abram travels through Canaan while building altars.

points.label: Source setting
points.left: Origins and call · Genesis 11:26–32
points.right: Origins and call · Genesis 12:1–9

compares.posture: Terah’s unfinished migration supplies the family setting for Abram’s own commanded departure.
compares.tension: The family travels toward Canaan and stops; Abram later leaves under a direct command whose destination is still only promised.
compares.title: Family movement and personal call

points.label: Repetition and difference
points.left: Famine leads Abram to Egypt, where speech about Sarai, household gain, plagues, confrontation, and expulsion follow.
points.right: Abraham again calls Sarah his sister; a dream, Abimelech’s questions, Abraham’s explanation, restoration, gifts, and prayer follow.

points.label: Source setting
points.left: Origins and call · Genesis 12:10–20
points.right: Hospitality and intercession · Genesis 20:1–18

compares.posture: Two royal households receive Sarah after Abraham uses sister-language.
compares.tension: The repeated concealment produces different warnings, replies, and endings.
compares.title: Egypt and Gerar

points.label: Choice and promise
points.left: Abram returns wealthy, worships at the earlier altar, addresses strife, and gives Lot the first choice of land.
points.right: After Lot separates, the LORD directs Abram’s sight across the land; Abram moves to Mamre and builds an altar.

points.label: Source setting
points.left: Land and neighbors · Genesis 13:1–13
points.right: Land and neighbors · Genesis 13:14–18

compares.posture: The land dispute and the renewed land speech meet at the moment Lot separates.
compares.tension: Human choice orders the separation; divine speech then directs Abram’s sight beyond that choice.
compares.title: Lot chooses and Abram looks

points.label: Outcome and possession
points.left: A regional war reaches Lot, and Abram responds with household forces and allies before bringing back people and goods.
points.right: Two kings meet Abram after the rescue: Melchizedek blesses and receives a tenth; Abram refuses the king of Sodom’s goods.

points.label: Source setting
points.left: Land and neighbors · Genesis 14:1–16
points.right: Land and neighbors · Genesis 14:17–24

compares.posture: The rescue of Lot leads directly to meetings with Melchizedek and the king of Sodom.
compares.tension: People and goods are recovered in the first source, then blessing, tenth, and refusal determine how the victory is received.
compares.title: Rescue and two royal encounters

points.label: Quotation and context
points.left: Abram answers the promise from his lack of an heir; the LORD directs him to the stars, and Abram believes.
points.right: Romans asks what Abraham found, contrasts work and gift, quotes belief being reckoned, and then cites David.

points.label: Source setting
points.left: Promise and household · Genesis 15:1–6
points.right: Gospel and apostolic memory · Romans 4:1–8

compares.posture: Romans explicitly quotes the Genesis statement about Abraham’s belief.
compares.tension: Genesis embeds the statement in childlessness and stars; Romans embeds it in work, gift, faith, and reckoning.
compares.title: Belief narrated and reckoning argued

points.label: Promise and later argument
points.left: Land, divided animals, darkness, the future of Abram’s offspring, and named boundaries gather in the covenant Scene.
points.right: Galatians examines promise, covenant, offspring, Christ, law, inheritance, and mediation.

points.label: Source setting
points.left: Promise and household · Genesis 15:7–21
points.right: Gospel and apostolic memory · Galatians 3:15–22

compares.posture: Galatians develops Abrahamic promise and offspring language from the Genesis covenant field.
compares.tension: Genesis narrates land, darkness, affliction, and boundaries; Galatians focuses on promise, offspring, law, and inheritance.
compares.title: Covenant land and promised offspring

points.label: Household and wilderness
points.left: Sarai gives Hagar to Abram, conflict follows conception, Hagar flees and receives speech, and Ishmael is born and named.
points.right: Sarah demands departure, Abraham is distressed, God speaks about both sons, and Hagar receives help after the water is gone.

points.label: Source setting
points.left: Promise and household · Genesis 16:1–16
points.right: Sons and testing · Genesis 21:9–21

compares.posture: Hagar’s two wilderness crises arise from Abraham’s household before and after Isaac’s birth.
compares.tension: The first follows conception and harsh treatment; the second follows inheritance conflict and expulsion.
compares.title: Hagar enters and Hagar departs

points.label: Sign and sequence
points.left: God names himself, renames Abram, speaks covenant and nations, and commands circumcision across the household.
points.right: Romans asks when Abraham’s faith was reckoned, calls circumcision a sign, and follows promise through hope, age, and resurrection language.

points.label: Source setting
points.left: Promise and household · Genesis 17:1–14
points.right: Gospel and apostolic memory · Romans 4:9–25

compares.posture: Romans explicitly examines when Abraham received the sign commanded in Genesis.
compares.tension: Genesis stresses household obligation; Romans stresses the order between reckoning and circumcision.
compares.title: Covenant sign and its sequence

leftEvidence.title: Sarah, Isaac, Ishmael, and the household

points.label: Speaker and response
points.left: Sarah is renamed, Isaac is promised, Abraham laughs and speaks about Ishmael, and the household is circumcised that day.
points.right: Abraham receives three visitors, the household prepares a meal, and renewed speech about Sarah’s son meets her laughter.

points.label: Source setting
points.left: Promise and household · Genesis 17:15–27
points.right: Hospitality and intercession · Genesis 18:1–15

compares.posture: The two adjacent promise scenes preserve different hearers, locations, and replies to birth speech.

rightEvidence.title: Visitors, a meal, and Sarah’s laughter

compares.tension: Both laugh inwardly, but the spoken responses and divine answers are not identical.
compares.title: Abraham laughs and Sarah laughs

points.label: Speech and silence
points.left: Speech about Sodom leads Abraham to ask repeatedly about the righteous and the city before the exchange ends.
points.right: Abraham returns to the place where he stood before the LORD, sees smoke, and the narration says God remembered him when Lot escaped.

points.label: Source setting
points.left: Hospitality and intercession · Genesis 18:16–33
points.right: Hospitality and intercession · Genesis 19:27–29

compares.posture: Abraham returns to the place of intercession after the cities are overthrown.
compares.tension: The first source contains sustained questions and replies; the second gives sight, smoke, and narrator explanation without Abraham’s words.
compares.title: Abraham speaks and Abraham sees

points.label: Fulfillment and threat
points.left: Sarah bears Isaac at the appointed time; Abraham names and circumcises him, and laughter returns at the weaning feast.
points.right: God names Isaac in a command, Abraham journeys and prepares the offering, the boy is spared, a ram is offered, and the promise is restated.

points.label: Source setting
points.left: Sons and testing · Genesis 21:1–8
points.right: Sons and testing · Genesis 22:1–19

compares.posture: The promised son’s birth makes the later command about the loved son materially charged.
compares.tension: Fulfillment and celebration stand beside a command to offer the same son before interruption and substitution.
compares.title: Isaac is born and Isaac is tested

leftEvidence.title: A well, an oath, and Beersheba

points.label: Oath and land
points.left: Abimelech seeks an oath; Abraham raises a seized well, sets witnesses, names Beersheba, plants a tree, and remains in the land.
points.right: During famine the LORD tells Isaac to remain in the land and recalls the oath and Abraham’s response.

points.label: Source setting
points.left: Sons and testing · Genesis 21:22–34
points.right: Family and Israel remember · Genesis 26:1–5

compares.posture: Abraham’s land dealings and the later oath speech to Isaac both concern residence before full possession.
compares.tension: One oath is made between human neighbors; the other is God’s ancestral oath recalled during famine.
compares.title: Oath at Beersheba and oath remembered

points.label: Preparation and recognition
points.left: After the return to Beersheba, Abraham hears the generations of Nahor, ending with the birth of Rebekah.
points.right: The servant prays for guidance, Rebekah waters the camels, and he blesses the God of Abraham after learning her family.

points.label: Source setting
points.left: Sons and testing · Genesis 22:20–24
points.right: Loss and final years · Genesis 24:10–28

compares.posture: The genealogy that names Rebekah prepares for the servant’s later meeting with her.
compares.tension: The first source reports kinship; the second tests recognition through action, prayer, and family identification.
compares.title: Rebekah named and Rebekah encountered

leftEvidence.title: Sarah dies; Abraham buys burial ground

points.label: Property and memory
points.left: Abraham mourns Sarah and negotiates publicly for the field and cave of Machpelah before burying her there.
points.right: Abraham dies at 175; Isaac and Ishmael bury him with Sarah in the purchased cave, and the narrative turns toward Isaac.

points.label: Source setting
points.left: Loss and final years · Genesis 23:1–20
points.right: Loss and final years · Genesis 25:7–11

compares.posture: The purchased cave joins Sarah’s burial to Abraham’s later burial.
compares.tension: The first source establishes legal possession through negotiation; the second returns Isaac and Ishmael to that same place.
compares.title: Burial ground purchased and reused

points.label: Command and retelling
points.left: In old age Abraham commissions his senior servant, distinguishes kinship from place, and refuses a return of Isaac to his former land.
points.right: Before Rebekah’s family the servant recounts Abraham’s commission and the well encounter; the family responds, Rebekah answers, and she leaves.

points.label: Source setting
points.left: Loss and final years · Genesis 24:1–9
points.right: Loss and final years · Genesis 24:29–61

compares.posture: The servant’s public account can be inspected against Abraham’s original private instructions.
compares.tension: The retelling preserves the mission while selecting and ordering details for Rebekah’s family.
compares.title: Commission given and commission retold

points.label: Household succession
points.left: Rebekah meets Isaac, the servant reports what happened, and Isaac brings her into Sarah’s tent and is comforted after his mother’s death.
points.right: Keturah and six sons are named before Abraham gives Isaac his estate and sends other sons east with gifts.

points.label: Source setting
points.left: Loss and final years · Genesis 24:62–67
points.right: Loss and final years · Genesis 25:1–6

compares.posture: Rebekah’s arrival and Abraham’s distribution of estate and gifts both prepare the family beyond Sarah’s death.
compares.tension: One source completes the servant’s mission around Isaac; the other orders Abraham’s wider descendants and inheritance.
compares.title: Isaac’s household and Abraham’s inheritance

leftEvidence.title: The God of Abraham speaks to Jacob

points.label: Promise and prayer
points.left: At Bethel Jacob hears the God of Abraham and Isaac speak of land, offspring, presence, protection, and return.
points.right: Facing Esau, Jacob addresses the God of Abraham and Isaac and repeats command, promise, fear, and offspring language.

points.label: Source setting
points.left: Family and Israel remember · Genesis 28:10–22
points.right: Family and Israel remember · Genesis 32:9–12

compares.posture: Jacob first hears the ancestral promise at Bethel and later invokes it in fear before meeting Esau.

rightEvidence.title: Jacob prays to the God of Abraham

compares.tension: The first source announces presence and return; the second turns command and promise into an appeal.
compares.title: Promise heard and promise invoked

points.label: Memory and action
points.left: God hears Israel’s groaning, remembers the covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, sees, and knows.
points.right: God tells Moses that Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob knew the divine appearance and joins their covenant to Israel’s coming deliverance.

points.label: Source setting
points.left: Family and Israel remember · Exodus 2:23–25
points.right: Family and Israel remember · Exodus 6:2–8

compares.posture: Both sources connect Abraham’s covenant to Israel’s distress in Egypt.
compares.tension: The first compresses hearing, remembering, seeing, and knowing; the second unfolds name, appearance, covenant, rescue, and land.
compares.title: Covenant remembered and deliverance announced

leftEvidence.title: The God of Abraham at the bush

points.label: Quotation and conclusion
points.left: At the bush God identifies himself through Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob before speaking of Israel’s suffering and deliverance.
points.right: A resurrection question leads Jesus to quote the bush identification and state that God is God of the living.

points.label: Source setting
points.left: Family and Israel remember · Exodus 3:1–8
points.right: Gospel and apostolic memory · Matthew 22:23–33

compares.posture: Jesus quotes the God-of-Abraham identification from the bush in a resurrection dispute.

rightEvidence.title: The God of Abraham and the living

compares.tension: Exodus introduces deliverance from Egypt; Matthew uses the divine name to argue about the living.
compares.title: The bush identification quoted

leftEvidence.title: Moses asks God to remember Abraham

points.label: Narration and retelling
points.left: After the calf, Moses appeals to God’s name among Egypt and to the oath sworn to Abraham, Isaac, and Israel.
points.right: Moses recounts forty days of intercession and asks the Lord to remember Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob rather than Israel’s resistance.

points.label: Source setting
points.left: Family and Israel remember · Exodus 32:11–14
points.right: Family and Israel remember · Deuteronomy 9:25–29

compares.posture: Deuteronomy retells Moses’ appeal after the calf and again names Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
compares.tension: The immediate account and later retelling share the ancestral appeal while arranging threat, reputation, and resistance differently.
compares.title: Moses invokes Abraham twice

points.label: Exile and entry
points.left: Confession, humbled hearts, ancestral covenant, land, exile, and the covenant made at the exodus are held together.
points.right: Moses tells Israel to leave Horeb and enter the land sworn to Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and their offspring.

points.label: Source setting
points.left: Family and Israel remember · Leviticus 26:40–45
points.right: Family and Israel remember · Deuteronomy 1:6–10

compares.posture: Both passages connect later Israel to the land sworn through Abraham.

rightEvidence.title: The oath and the land before Israel

compares.tension: Leviticus speaks from confession and exile; Deuteronomy speaks from departure toward the land.
compares.title: Covenant remembered and land entered

points.label: Retelling and location
points.left: Joshua’s assembly hears Abraham’s family placed beyond the River before God takes, leads, and gives descendants.
points.right: Stephen recounts Mesopotamia, Haran, land without inheritance, offspring, foreign affliction, covenant, and Isaac.

points.label: Source setting
points.left: Family and Israel remember · Joshua 24:1–5
points.right: Gospel and apostolic memory · Acts 7:1–8

compares.posture: Joshua and Stephen both retell Abraham’s origins and divine movement across places.
compares.tension: Joshua begins beyond the River among other gods; Stephen locates appearance, Haran, no foothold, future affliction, and covenant.
compares.title: Abraham’s call retold twice

leftEvidence.title: Abram chosen and renamed in prayer

points.label: Selection and memory
points.left: The prayer names choosing Abram, bringing him from Ur, renaming him, finding his heart faithful, and making covenant.
points.right: Hebrews recalls Abraham’s departure, unknown destination, foreign residence, tents, city, and Sarah’s reception of power.

points.label: Source setting
points.left: Family and Israel remember · Nehemiah 9:5–8
points.right: Gospel and apostolic memory · Hebrews 11:8–12

compares.posture: A corporate prayer and Hebrews both remember Abraham’s departure under divine initiative.
compares.tension: Nehemiah emphasizes choosing, renaming, faithfulness, and covenant; Hebrews emphasizes obedience, uncertainty, tents, and expectation.
compares.title: Abram chosen and Abraham going out

points.label: Memory and mercy
points.left: The psalm calls for seeking and remembering, then names covenant with Abraham, oath to Isaac, and land to Israel.
points.right: Micah closes with pardon language and names truth to Jacob and mercy to Abraham tied to the ancestral oath.

points.label: Source setting
points.left: Family and Israel remember · Psalms 105:4–11
points.right: Family and Israel remember · Micah 7:18–20

compares.posture: Both texts place Abraham inside communal speech about remembered covenant faithfulness.
compares.tension: The psalm commands remembrance and names land; Micah closes with pardon, mercy, truth, and oath.
compares.title: Covenant in song and prophetic prayer

points.label: Name and argument
points.left: Israel is addressed as servant, chosen offspring, and descendant of Abraham before receiving words against fear.
points.right: James recalls Abraham offering Isaac, joins faith with works, quotes reckoning, and names friendship with God.

points.label: Source setting
points.left: Family and Israel remember · Isaiah 41:8–10
points.right: Gospel and apostolic memory · James 2:20–24

compares.posture: Isaiah’s friend language reappears in James after belief and altar action are joined.
compares.tension: Isaiah addresses Israel through Abraham; James uses Abraham to reason about faith and works.
compares.title: Abraham called friend

points.label: Descent and divine action
points.left: Hearers are told to look to the rock, Abraham, and Sarah while one called person becomes many and Zion’s waste becomes garden.
points.right: John challenges reliance on Abrahamic descent while speaking of fruit, stones, trees, and judgment.

points.label: Source setting
points.left: Family and Israel remember · Isaiah 51:1–3
points.right: Gospel and apostolic memory · Matthew 3:7–10

compares.posture: Isaiah and John both unsettle simple confidence in present numbers or inherited descent.
compares.tension: Isaiah uses Abraham and Sarah to encourage Zion; John uses Abraham and stones to challenge unfruitful ancestry claims.
compares.title: One became many and stones could become children

points.label: Portrait and example
points.left: Sirach places Abraham’s covenant, testing, faithfulness, blessing, land, Isaac, and Jacob within an ancestral portrait.
points.right: Mattathias calls his sons to remember earlier generations and names Abraham among a sequence of tested ancestors.

points.label: Source setting
points.left: Family and Israel remember · Sirach 44:19–23
points.right: Family and Israel remember · 1 Maccabees 2:50–54

compares.posture: Both later Jewish texts present Abraham within a selective memory of faithful ancestors.

rightEvidence.title: Abraham remembered as faithful in testing

compares.tension: Sirach gives a sustained portrait; 1 Maccabees compresses Abraham into one example within a crisis speech.
compares.title: Abraham in two ancestral appeals

points.label: Genealogy and proclamation
points.left: Matthew introduces Jesus through David and Abraham, then begins the generations with Abraham and Isaac.
points.right: Zechariah’s prophecy joins visitation, redemption, covenant memory, and the oath sworn to Abraham.

points.label: Source setting
points.left: Gospel and apostolic memory · Matthew 1:1–4
points.right: Gospel and apostolic memory · Luke 1:67–75

compares.posture: Matthew’s genealogy and Luke’s song both place Abraham near the opening of their Gospel narratives.

rightEvidence.title: The oath to Abraham in Zechariah’s song

compares.tension: One orders descent through repeated fathering; the other interprets present events through covenant and oath.
compares.title: Abraham at two Gospel openings

points.label: Belonging and reversal
points.left: A centurion speaks about authority; Jesus responds with astonishment and names many sitting with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
points.right: The rich man and Lazarus die; Abraham answers across a fixed gulf and speaks about memory, Moses, the prophets, and persuasion.

points.label: Source setting
points.left: Gospel and apostolic memory · Matthew 8:5–13
points.right: Gospel and apostolic memory · Luke 16:19–31

compares.posture: Jesus’ teaching uses Abraham in two scenes about belonging and reversal.
compares.tension: Matthew pictures many reclining with the patriarchs; Luke’s parable places Abraham across an impassable gulf.
compares.title: Abraham at a future table and across a fixed gulf

points.label: Identity and response
points.left: Jesus heals a bent woman on the Sabbath and answers the synagogue ruler by naming her a daughter of Abraham.
points.right: After Zacchaeus receives Jesus and speaks about his possessions, Jesus calls him a son of Abraham and names salvation.

points.label: Source setting
points.left: Gospel and apostolic memory · Luke 13:10–17
points.right: Gospel and apostolic memory · Luke 19:1–10

compares.posture: Luke applies Abrahamic family language to two people under public objection.
compares.tension: The woman is released on the Sabbath; Zacchaeus receives Jesus, names restitution, and is called a son when salvation is announced.
compares.title: Daughter of Abraham and son of Abraham

points.label: Claim and escalation
points.left: A dispute about freedom, ancestry, hearing, and action tests the claim that Abraham is father.
points.right: The dispute turns from insult and death to Abraham’s rejoicing, age, existence, stones, and departure.

points.label: Source setting
points.left: Gospel and apostolic memory · John 8:31–47
points.right: Gospel and apostolic memory · John 8:48–59

compares.posture: One continuous dispute moves from claims of ancestry to claims about Abraham seeing Jesus’ day.
compares.tension: The first part tests kinship through action; the second presses honor, death, seeing, age, and existence.
compares.title: Abrahamic works and Abraham’s rejoicing

points.label: Promise and address
points.left: Peter joins Moses’ prophet saying to the covenant with Abraham and addresses his hearers as its children.
points.right: Galatians quotes Abraham’s belief and the blessing of nations while contrasting faith, law, curse, and blessing.

points.label: Source setting
points.left: Gospel and apostolic memory · Acts 3:22–26
points.right: Gospel and apostolic memory · Galatians 3:6–14

compares.posture: Peter and Paul both use Abraham’s blessing language in addresses about present response.
compares.tension: Acts joins the covenant to prophetic sending and turning; Galatians joins it to faith, curse, and redemption.
compares.title: Covenant children and nations blessed

points.label: Descent and belonging
points.left: Romans distinguishes physical descent from children of promise while quoting the word about Sarah and a son.
points.right: Those baptized into Christ are addressed across social distinctions and then called Abraham’s offspring and heirs.

points.label: Source setting
points.left: Gospel and apostolic memory · Romans 9:6–9
points.right: Gospel and apostolic memory · Galatians 3:27–29

compares.posture: Romans and Galatians both distinguish Abrahamic belonging from unexamined physical descent.
compares.tension: Romans focuses on the promised line through Isaac; Galatians names belonging to Christ and heirship.
compares.title: Children of promise and Abraham’s offspring

leftEvidence.title: Hagar and Sarah in a later argument

points.label: Narrative and allegory
points.left: Galatians names Abraham’s two sons and mothers, then explicitly marks its reading as allegorical while contrasting two covenants.
points.right: Sarah demands departure, Abraham is distressed, God speaks about both sons, and Hagar receives help after the water is gone.

points.label: Source setting
points.left: Gospel and apostolic memory · Galatians 4:21–31
points.right: Sons and testing · Genesis 21:9–21

compares.posture: Galatians explicitly rereads Abraham’s two sons and mothers from the Genesis household crisis.
compares.tension: Genesis narrates distress, departure, danger, and rescue; Galatians maps the relationships into an allegorical covenant argument.
compares.title: Household narrated and household reread

points.label: Promise and assurance
points.left: Hebrews recalls God’s promise and oath to Abraham before speaking of confirmation, hope, and the inner sanctuary.
points.right: Land, divided animals, darkness, the future of Abram’s offspring, and named boundaries gather in the covenant Scene.

points.label: Source setting
points.left: Gospel and apostolic memory · Hebrews 6:13–20
points.right: Promise and household · Genesis 15:7–21

compares.posture: Hebrews makes God’s promise and oath to Abraham grounds for later hope.
compares.tension: Genesis sets promise within covenant ritual and future affliction; Hebrews emphasizes confirmation and refuge.
compares.title: Promise given and oath remembered

points.label: Narrative and analysis
points.left: Hebrews retells the meeting, blessing, and tenth while drawing attention to names, genealogy, greatness, and Levi.
points.right: Two kings meet Abram after the rescue: Melchizedek blesses and receives a tenth; Abram refuses the king of Sodom’s goods.

points.label: Source setting
points.left: Gospel and apostolic memory · Hebrews 7:1–10
points.right: Land and neighbors · Genesis 14:17–24

compares.posture: Hebrews explicitly returns to Abraham’s meeting with Melchizedek.
compares.tension: Genesis supplies encounter, blessing, tenth, and Sodom’s king; Hebrews selects and analyzes names, genealogy, blessing, and greatness.
compares.title: Meeting narrated and meeting analyzed

points.label: Narrative and interpretation
points.left: Hebrews recalls Abraham offering Isaac while holding the only son, promises, offspring saying, and resurrection reasoning together.
points.right: God names Isaac in a command, Abraham journeys and prepares the offering, the boy is spared, a ram is offered, and the promise is restated.

points.label: Source setting
points.left: Gospel and apostolic memory · Hebrews 11:17–19
points.right: Sons and testing · Genesis 22:1–19

compares.posture: Hebrews explicitly remembers Abraham offering Isaac.
compares.tension: Genesis gives the journey, dialogue, interruption, substitute, and renewed promise; Hebrews supplies resurrection reasoning.
compares.title: Testing narrated and remembered

leftEvidence.title: Sarah and Abraham in household speech

points.label: Selection and narrative
points.left: First Peter names Sarah’s response to Abraham inside an address about conduct, adornment, hope, fear, knowledge, and honor.
points.right: Abraham receives three visitors, the household prepares a meal, and renewed speech about Sarah’s son meets her laughter.

points.label: Source setting
points.left: Gospel and apostolic memory · 1 Peter 3:1–7
points.right: Hospitality and intercession · Genesis 18:1–15

compares.posture: First Peter selects Sarah’s relation to Abraham while Genesis shows her inside a visitor and promise scene.

rightEvidence.title: Visitors, a meal, and Sarah’s laughter

compares.tension: The later address uses a narrow household example; Genesis preserves laughter, fear, overheard speech, and reply.
compares.title: Sarah remembered and Sarah narrated

dissects.title: Named in Terah’s family

edges.basis: Genesis 11:26–32 ↔ Genesis 12:1–9: Terah’s unfinished migration supplies the family setting for Abram’s own commanded departure.
edges.label: Family movement and personal call

edges.basis: Genesis 12:10–20 ↔ Genesis 20:1–18: Two royal households receive Sarah after Abraham uses sister-language.
edges.label: Egypt and Gerar

edges.basis: Genesis 13:1–13 ↔ Genesis 13:14–18: The land dispute and the renewed land speech meet at the moment Lot separates.
edges.label: Lot chooses and Abram looks

edges.basis: Genesis 14:1–16 ↔ Genesis 14:17–24: The rescue of Lot leads directly to meetings with Melchizedek and the king of Sodom.
edges.label: Rescue and two royal encounters

edges.basis: Genesis 15:1–6 ↔ Romans 4:1–8: Romans explicitly quotes the Genesis statement about Abraham’s belief.
edges.label: Belief narrated and reckoning argued

edges.basis: Genesis 15:7–21 ↔ Galatians 3:15–22: Galatians develops Abrahamic promise and offspring language from the Genesis covenant field.
edges.label: Covenant land and promised offspring

edges.basis: Genesis 16:1–16 ↔ Genesis 21:9–21: Hagar’s two wilderness crises arise from Abraham’s household before and after Isaac’s birth.
edges.label: Hagar enters and Hagar departs

edges.basis: Genesis 17:1–14 ↔ Romans 4:9–25: Romans explicitly examines when Abraham received the sign commanded in Genesis.
edges.label: Covenant sign and its sequence

edges.basis: Genesis 17:15–27 ↔ Genesis 18:1–15: The two adjacent promise scenes preserve different hearers, locations, and replies to birth speech.
edges.label: Abraham laughs and Sarah laughs

edges.basis: Genesis 18:16–33 ↔ Genesis 19:27–29: Abraham returns to the place of intercession after the cities are overthrown.
edges.label: Abraham speaks and Abraham sees

edges.basis: Genesis 21:1–8 ↔ Genesis 22:1–19: The promised son’s birth makes the later command about the loved son materially charged.
edges.label: Isaac is born and Isaac is tested

edges.basis: Genesis 21:22–34 ↔ Genesis 26:1–5: Abraham’s land dealings and the later oath speech to Isaac both concern residence before full possession.
edges.label: Oath at Beersheba and oath remembered

edges.basis: Genesis 22:20–24 ↔ Genesis 24:10–28: The genealogy that names Rebekah prepares for the servant’s later meeting with her.
edges.label: Rebekah named and Rebekah encountered

edges.basis: Genesis 23:1–20 ↔ Genesis 25:7–11: The purchased cave joins Sarah’s burial to Abraham’s later burial.
edges.label: Burial ground purchased and reused

edges.basis: Genesis 24:1–9 ↔ Genesis 24:29–61: The servant’s public account can be inspected against Abraham’s original private instructions.
edges.label: Commission given and commission retold

edges.basis: Genesis 24:62–67 ↔ Genesis 25:1–6: Rebekah’s arrival and Abraham’s distribution of estate and gifts both prepare the family beyond Sarah’s death.
edges.label: Isaac’s household and Abraham’s inheritance

edges.basis: Genesis 28:10–22 ↔ Genesis 32:9–12: Jacob first hears the ancestral promise at Bethel and later invokes it in fear before meeting Esau.
edges.label: Promise heard and promise invoked

edges.basis: Exodus 2:23–25 ↔ Exodus 6:2–8: Both sources connect Abraham’s covenant to Israel’s distress in Egypt.
edges.label: Covenant remembered and deliverance announced

edges.basis: Exodus 3:1–8 ↔ Matthew 22:23–33: Jesus quotes the God-of-Abraham identification from the bush in a resurrection dispute.
edges.label: The bush identification quoted

edges.basis: Exodus 32:11–14 ↔ Deuteronomy 9:25–29: Deuteronomy retells Moses’ appeal after the calf and again names Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
edges.label: Moses invokes Abraham twice

edges.basis: Leviticus 26:40–45 ↔ Deuteronomy 1:6–10: Both passages connect later Israel to the land sworn through Abraham.
edges.label: Covenant remembered and land entered

edges.basis: Joshua 24:1–5 ↔ Acts 7:1–8: Joshua and Stephen both retell Abraham’s origins and divine movement across places.
edges.label: Abraham’s call retold twice

edges.basis: Nehemiah 9:5–8 ↔ Hebrews 11:8–12: A corporate prayer and Hebrews both remember Abraham’s departure under divine initiative.
edges.label: Abram chosen and Abraham going out

edges.basis: Psalms 105:4–11 ↔ Micah 7:18–20: Both texts place Abraham inside communal speech about remembered covenant faithfulness.
edges.label: Covenant in song and prophetic prayer

edges.basis: Isaiah 41:8–10 ↔ James 2:20–24: Isaiah’s friend language reappears in James after belief and altar action are joined.
edges.label: Abraham called friend

edges.basis: Isaiah 51:1–3 ↔ Matthew 3:7–10: Isaiah and John both unsettle simple confidence in present numbers or inherited descent.
edges.label: One became many and stones could become children

edges.basis: Sirach 44:19–23 ↔ 1 Maccabees 2:50–54: Both later Jewish texts present Abraham within a selective memory of faithful ancestors.
edges.label: Abraham in two ancestral appeals

edges.basis: Matthew 1:1–4 ↔ Luke 1:67–75: Matthew’s genealogy and Luke’s song both place Abraham near the opening of their Gospel narratives.
edges.label: Abraham at two Gospel openings

edges.basis: Matthew 8:5–13 ↔ Luke 16:19–31: Jesus’ teaching uses Abraham in two scenes about belonging and reversal.
edges.label: Abraham at a future table and across a fixed gulf

edges.basis: Luke 13:10–17 ↔ Luke 19:1–10: Luke applies Abrahamic family language to two people under public objection.
edges.label: Daughter of Abraham and son of Abraham

edges.basis: John 8:31–47 ↔ John 8:48–59: One continuous dispute moves from claims of ancestry to claims about Abraham seeing Jesus’ day.
edges.label: Abrahamic works and Abraham’s rejoicing

edges.basis: Acts 3:22–26 ↔ Galatians 3:6–14: Peter and Paul both use Abraham’s blessing language in addresses about present response.
edges.label: Covenant children and nations blessed

edges.basis: Romans 9:6–9 ↔ Galatians 3:27–29: Romans and Galatians both distinguish Abrahamic belonging from unexamined physical descent.
edges.label: Children of promise and Abraham’s offspring

edges.basis: Galatians 4:21–31 ↔ Genesis 21:9–21: Galatians explicitly rereads Abraham’s two sons and mothers from the Genesis household crisis.
edges.label: Household narrated and household reread

edges.basis: Hebrews 6:13–20 ↔ Genesis 15:7–21: Hebrews makes God’s promise and oath to Abraham grounds for later hope.
edges.label: Promise given and oath remembered

edges.basis: Hebrews 7:1–10 ↔ Genesis 14:17–24: Hebrews explicitly returns to Abraham’s meeting with Melchizedek.
edges.label: Meeting narrated and meeting analyzed

edges.basis: Hebrews 11:17–19 ↔ Genesis 22:1–19: Hebrews explicitly remembers Abraham offering Isaac.
edges.label: Testing narrated and remembered

edges.basis: 1 Peter 3:1–7 ↔ Genesis 18:1–15: First Peter selects Sarah’s relation to Abraham while Genesis shows her inside a visitor and promise scene.
edges.label: Sarah remembered and Sarah narrated

topic.orientation: Do not reduce Abraham to one virtue, failure, promise, or later argument. Follow his relationships, movements, decisions, questions, losses, and later Scripture memory as they accumulate.

passages.excerpt: Terah lived seventy years, and became the father of Abram, Nahor, and Haran.
passages.observation: Abram is named with Nahor and Haran before Terah’s household moves from Ur toward Canaan and settles in Haran.
passages.title: Named in Terah’s family

passages.excerpt: Now the LORD said to Abram, “Leave your country, and your relatives, and your father’s house, and go to the land that I will show you.
passages.observation: The LORD commands Abram to leave, speaks blessing, and Abram travels through Canaan while building altars.
passages.title: Leave your country

passages.excerpt: When he had come near to enter Egypt, he said to Sarai his wife, “See now, I know that you are a beautiful woman to look at.
passages.observation: Famine leads Abram to Egypt, where speech about Sarai, household gain, plagues, confrontation, and expulsion follow.
passages.title: Famine and Pharaoh

passages.excerpt: Lot also, who went with Abram, had flocks, herds, and tents.
passages.observation: Abram returns wealthy, worships at the earlier altar, addresses strife, and gives Lot the first choice of land.
passages.title: Return and separation

passages.excerpt: The LORD said to Abram, after Lot was separated from him, “Now, lift up your eyes, and look from the place where you are, northward and southward and eastward and…
passages.observation: After Lot separates, the LORD directs Abram’s sight across the land; Abram moves to Mamre and builds an altar.
passages.title: Look from where you are

passages.excerpt: They took Lot, Abram’s brother’s son, who lived in Sodom, and his goods, and departed.
passages.observation: A regional war reaches Lot, and Abram responds with household forces and allies before bringing back people and goods.
passages.title: Lot taken; Abram pursues

passages.excerpt: Melchizedek king of Salem brought out bread and wine. He was priest of God Most High.
passages.observation: Two kings meet Abram after the rescue: Melchizedek blesses and receives a tenth; Abram refuses the king of Sodom’s goods.
passages.title: Blessing, tenth, and refusal

passages.excerpt: After these things the LORD’s word came to Abram in a vision, saying, “Don’t be afraid, Abram. I am your shield, your exceedingly great reward.”
passages.observation: Abram answers the promise from his lack of an heir; the LORD directs him to the stars, and Abram believes.
passages.title: Childlessness and the stars

passages.excerpt: He said to Abram, “I am the LORD who brought you out of Ur of the Chaldees, to give you this land to inherit it.”
passages.observation: Land, divided animals, darkness, the future of Abram’s offspring, and named boundaries gather in the covenant Scene.
passages.title: Land, darkness, and covenant

passages.excerpt: Now Sarai, Abram’s wife, bore him no children. She had a servant, an Egyptian, whose name was Hagar.
passages.observation: Sarai gives Hagar to Abram, conflict follows conception, Hagar flees and receives speech, and Ishmael is born and named.
passages.title: Sarai, Hagar, and Ishmael

passages.excerpt: When Abram was ninety-nine years old, the LORD appeared to Abram and said to him, “I am God Almighty. Walk before me and be blameless.
passages.observation: God names himself, renames Abram, speaks covenant and nations, and commands circumcision across the household.
passages.title: Abram renamed; covenant marked

passages.excerpt: God said to Abraham, “As for Sarai your wife, you shall not call her name Sarai, but her name shall be Sarah.
passages.observation: Sarah is renamed, Isaac is promised, Abraham laughs and speaks about Ishmael, and the household is circumcised that day.
passages.title: Sarah, Isaac, Ishmael, and the household

passages.excerpt: The LORD appeared to him by the oaks of Mamre, as he sat in the tent door in the heat of the day.
passages.observation: Abraham receives three visitors, the household prepares a meal, and renewed speech about Sarah’s son meets her laughter.
passages.title: Visitors, a meal, and Sarah’s laughter

passages.excerpt: The men rose up from there, and looked toward Sodom. Abraham went with them to see them on their way.
passages.observation: Speech about Sodom leads Abraham to ask repeatedly about the righteous and the city before the exchange ends.
passages.title: Abraham stands and speaks

passages.excerpt: Abraham went up early in the morning to the place where he had stood before the LORD.
passages.observation: Abraham returns to the place where he stood before the LORD, sees smoke, and the narration says God remembered him when Lot escaped.
passages.title: Abraham looks toward the plain

passages.excerpt: Abraham traveled from there toward the land of the South, and lived between Kadesh and Shur. He lived as a foreigner in Gerar.
passages.observation: Abraham again calls Sarah his sister; a dream, Abimelech’s questions, Abraham’s explanation, restoration, gifts, and prayer follow.
passages.title: Sarah in Gerar

passages.excerpt: The LORD visited Sarah as he had said, and the LORD did to Sarah as he had spoken.
passages.observation: Sarah bears Isaac at the appointed time; Abraham names and circumcises him, and laughter returns at the weaning feast.
passages.title: Isaac is born and named

passages.excerpt: Sarah saw the son of Hagar the Egyptian, whom she had borne to Abraham, mocking.
passages.observation: Sarah demands departure, Abraham is distressed, God speaks about both sons, and Hagar receives help after the water is gone.
passages.title: Hagar and Ishmael sent away

passages.excerpt: At that time, Abimelech and Phicol the captain of his army spoke to Abraham, saying, “God is with you in all that you do.
passages.observation: Abimelech seeks an oath; Abraham raises a seized well, sets witnesses, names Beersheba, plants a tree, and remains in the land.
passages.title: A well, an oath, and Beersheba

passages.excerpt: After these things, God tested Abraham, and said to him, “Abraham!” He said, “Here I am.”
passages.observation: God names Isaac in a command, Abraham journeys and prepares the offering, the boy is spared, a ram is offered, and the promise is restated.
passages.title: Abraham is tested

passages.excerpt: After these things, Abraham was told, “Behold, Milcah, she also has borne children to your brother Nahor:
passages.observation: After the return to Beersheba, Abraham hears the generations of Nahor, ending with the birth of Rebekah.
passages.title: Rebekah named in Nahor’s house

passages.excerpt: Sarah lived one hundred twenty-seven years. This was the length of Sarah’s life.
passages.observation: Abraham mourns Sarah and negotiates publicly for the field and cave of Machpelah before burying her there.
passages.title: Sarah dies; Abraham buys burial ground

passages.excerpt: Abraham was old, and well advanced in age. The LORD had blessed Abraham in all things.
